Give floor2 a short projecting side wing, a recessed full-height window and an offset supported balcony. Floor3 is a NARROWER NONRESIDENTIAL MACHINE FLOOR, made of a load-bearing open frame, two large recovered retro-futurist equipment casings, an inset maintenance aisle and thick functional connections. Floor4 is a WIDER occupied volume overhanging floor3 on both visible sides, with a large rounded projecting window enclosure and an asymmetrical end. Make 1<2 and 3<4 footprints unmistakable, no extra inhabited floor. Keep substantial recesses, support beams and visible undersides, rather than four similar boxes.
buildings.B: Building B: exactly TWO storeys. Floor1 IS a substantial retro-futurist mechanical structure, not a normal shop with devices attached: two different bulky rounded appliance-like power housings, thick support frame, deep service slot and a closed human access door integrated into the service core. Give it a curved end, deep window and side maintenance deck. Its silhouette differs strongly from A.

exits: Two buildings at the rear, with substantial connected utility walls completing the two rear blocking boundaries. Exactly TWO map exits, one clear passage through each rear boundary direction (back-left and back-right), visibly connected to open space beyond. Put one between a building and a broad service wall, the other alongside a low utility gantry. No duplicated door arches. Building entry doors are closed human-sized doors, separate from the two open exits. Keep the central street and approaches to both exits continuous, unobstructed and grounded with readable footings, supports, threshold heights and headroom. No tall front fence. No exposed interior rooms. The buildings' straight structures share the ground X/Y axes; coherent rounded cladding is allowed, but no arbitrarily rotated buildings or tight wedge gaps.

Intact walls, rounded painted metal casings, vehicles, pale paving and asphalt each show sparse BROAD FLAT DIRECTIONAL brush swipes of closely neighboring hue/value, clearly visible independently of damage. Use smooth broad brush edges and large quiet intervals. These pigment swipes are neither chipped paint nor rust, dirt, little scratches or raised relief. Keep most wall color intact, only a few large localized worn/repair patches. No granular noise, stippling, small evenly scattered marks, mosaic fragments or photoreal miniature texture. Preserve deep architecture and thick mechanical volumes despite calm surfaces. Warm daylight plus soft cool skylight, one coherent shadow direction, readable metal/plaster/glass through broad material responses.
